name: wifi_status
summary: Report the Wi-Fi radio's power state, the network it is currently joined to (if any), and that connection's signal strength (RSSI in dBm, with a plain-language quality rating). Answers 'what Wi-Fi am I on?' and 'is my signal any good?'.

name: list_preferred_wifi
summary: List the preferred (remembered) Wi-Fi networks this Mac auto-joins, in priority order. Listing nearby/available networks isn't supported (needs elevated privileges) — use open_settings (pane 'wifi') to pick a new one.

name: bluetooth_status
summary: Report whether Bluetooth is on, which devices are currently connected, and which are paired but not connected. Turning Bluetooth on/off has no first-party command line on macOS — use open_settings (pane 'bluetooth').

name: power_status
summary: Report power and battery state: the current power source, battery charge and charging status, whether Low Power Mode is on, and battery health (condition, cycle count, maximum capacity) on machines with a battery.

name: about_this_mac
summary: Report what this Mac is: macOS version and build, model, chip/CPU, core count, memory, and serial number.

name: uptime
summary: Report how long this Mac has been running since its last boot (plus load averages).

name: disk_usage
summary: Report every mounted volume with its total size, used space, and free space (what Finder shows, in SI units).

name: software_update_check
summary: Check Apple's update service for pending macOS/software updates (read-only — never downloads or installs; installing is an open_settings hand-off). Contacts Apple's servers and can take up to a minute.

name: list_airplay_devices
summary: List AirPlay receivers (Apple TVs, AirPlay-capable TVs/speakers, other Macs) reachable on the local network right now — answers 'what can I mirror or stream to?'. Read-only discovery; it does NOT start mirroring (there is no command line to begin it) — hand that off with open_settings (pane 'displays'). May be empty if no receivers are on, and the host app may need Local Network access on first use.

name: list_input_sources
summary: List the enabled keyboard layouts and input methods (typing languages) and mark which one is currently active — answers 'what can I type in?'. Read-only. Adding/removing a language or switching the active source has no command line; hand that off with open_settings (pane 'keyboard').

name: open_settings
summary: Open a specific pane of System Settings. Use to hand off actions this server can't do directly — because they need admin rights (connecting/re-enabling a printer, joining a Wi-Fi network, battery/Low-Power settings, turning a sharing service on or off) or have no command line at all (pairing a Bluetooth device, signing into iCloud, toggling a Focus, adding a keyboard language, starting screen mirroring). ALWAYS tell the user the exact click-path to finish in the opened pane — e.g. bluetooth: 'put the device in pairing mode, then click Connect next to it under Nearby Devices'; apple_id: 'sign in or manage iCloud here'; focus: 'turn a Focus like Do Not Disturb on or off here'; keyboard: 'Text Input > Input Sources > Edit, then + to add a language'; displays: 'the AirPlay/mirroring control is the + dropdown here'; sharing: 'toggle Remote Login, Screen Sharing, or File Sharing here'. Runs immediately; cannot be undone (it just opens a window).

params.name: pane
params.description: Which System Settings pane to open. 'focus' = Focus/Do Not Disturb; 'keyboard' = keyboard and input sources (add/change a typing language); 'apple_id' = Apple Account / iCloud; 'displays' = display arrangement and AirPlay screen mirroring; 'sharing' = Sharing (Remote Login/SSH, Screen Sharing, File Sharing toggles).

name: notify
summary: Post a macOS notification banner to get the user's attention — e.g. to signal that a long-running task finished or that you need input. Runs immediately; cannot be undone (a shown notification can't be recalled). If nothing appears, the host app needs Notifications enabled in System Settings > Notifications.

params.name: title
params.description: The bold title line shown above the message.

name: speak
summary: Speak text aloud through the Mac's speakers using the system voice (text-to-speech). Use to get the user's attention audibly. Runs immediately; cannot be undone (audio plays at once). Text is capped at 2000 characters.

params.name: text
params.description: The text to speak aloud (up to 2000 characters).

name: display_sleep
summary: Put the display(s) to sleep immediately (turn the screen off) without sleeping the whole Mac. Runs immediately; cannot be undone from software — waking the screen is a manual action (press a key or move the mouse). Does not lock the Mac or stop any running work.

name: wifi_set_power
summary: Turn the Wi-Fi radio on or off. Staged for confirmation because turning Wi-Fi off disconnects this Mac from any Wi-Fi network. Reversible: undo restores the previous power state. To JOIN a specific network (rather than toggle the radio) there is no non-admin command — use open_settings (pane 'wifi').

params.name: power
params.description: Whether to turn the Wi-Fi radio 'on' or 'off'.

name: keep_awake
summary: Keep this Mac awake for a set time — block display sleep and idle system sleep (e.g. during a long download or presentation). Staged for confirmation because it changes power behaviour for up to hours. The session stops on its own when the timer expires; there is no automatic undo — end it early with allow_sleep. To see what is currently keeping the Mac awake, use sleep_assertions.

params.name: duration_seconds
params.description: How long to keep the Mac awake, in seconds (60 to 14400, i.e. 1 minute to 4 hours). Defaults to 3600 (1 hour).

name: allow_sleep
summary: End any keep-awake session so this Mac can sleep normally again. Cancels the keep_awake sessions this user started (by stopping their caffeinate helpers). Runs immediately; cannot be undone (start a new session with keep_awake if needed). If no session is active, it reports that nothing needed changing.

name: sleep_assertions
summary: Report what is currently keeping this Mac awake: which sleep-preventing power assertions are active (idle system sleep, display sleep, ...) and which processes are holding them (e.g. a caffeinate session, a video call, a download). Read-only — answers 'why won't my Mac sleep?'.

name: system_log
summary: Show a recent slice of the unified system log (what macOS and its apps have been recording), optionally narrowed to one process and/or subsystem. Answers 'what's spamming the log?' and 'what did app X just report?'. Read-only. Covers the last few minutes only (1–30); an unfiltered window can be large and is truncated to fit — narrow it with 'process' and/or 'subsystem' to see more of what you care about.

params.name: duration_minutes
params.description: How far back to look, in minutes (1–30). Defaults to 5. Smaller windows return faster and are less likely to be truncated.

params.name: process
params.description: Optional: show only entries logged by this process/app (e.g. 'Safari', 'bluetoothd'). Matched exactly against the process name.

params.name: subsystem
params.description: Optional: show only entries from this logging subsystem, a reverse-DNS identifier (e.g. 'com.apple.wifi'). Combined with 'process' when both are given.

name: thermal_state
summary: Report whether the CPU is currently being throttled to manage heat (thermal pressure), read from pmset. Answers 'why is my Mac suddenly slow or hot?' — a CPU speed limit below 100% means macOS is clamping performance to cool down. Read-only.

name: remap_key
summary: Remap a keyboard modifier key to a common alternative — e.g. make Caps Lock act as Escape or Control, swap the Command and Option keys, or disable Caps Lock entirely. Only a fixed menu of vetted remaps is offered (you cannot supply an arbitrary mapping). Staged for confirmation because it changes how the keyboard behaves. Reversible: undo restores whatever mapping was in effect before. NOTE: hidutil remaps do NOT survive a reboot (macOS clears UserKeyMapping on restart) — to make one permanent the user must set it up as a login item themselves. Use key_remap_status to see the current mapping.

params.name: remap
params.description: Which vetted remap to apply. 'caps_lock_to_escape' = Caps Lock types Escape; 'caps_lock_to_control' = Caps Lock acts as Control; 'swap_command_option' = swap the Command and Option keys (both sides); 'swap_control_command' = swap the Control and Command keys (both sides); 'disable_caps_lock' = Caps Lock does nothing.

name: key_remap_status
summary: Report the keyboard key remapping currently in effect (macOS's hidutil UserKeyMapping) — answers 'is Caps Lock remapped right now?'. Read-only. Names the remap when it matches a known one (e.g. Caps Lock → Escape), otherwise lists the raw source→destination key pairs. Reports 'no custom remapping' when the keyboard is at its defaults. Remaps set via remap_key are cleared by a reboot.

name: sharing_status
summary: Report whether this Mac's main sharing services are turned on: Remote Login (SSH), Screen Sharing, and File Sharing. Answers 'is screen sharing on?' / 'can someone SSH into my Mac?'. Read-only — it detects each service by checking whether the Mac is listening on that service's port (22, 5900, 445) on its own loopback interface. To turn any of them on or off, use open_settings (pane 'sharing').
